Some upgrades you only really appreciate on day three of a trip — when you're rummaging for clean socks or trying to find the head torch. The Rear Pull-Out Drawer Storage System is one of those.

Over 330 litres of organised, accessible storage, sliding straight out through the rear doors. Heavy-duty runners rated to 220 kg — enough for boots, sleeping bags, wetsuits, tools, and whatever else gets thrown in at the last minute. Laser-cut and folded aluminium with a CNC-cut phenolic plywood front panel and lid. The lid doubles as a useful prep surface when the drawer is closed.

Designed to fit VW T5, T6, T6.1, and the Ford Transit Custom — no compromises on capacity or build quality.

Link in bio for full specs and to order.

A safety detail that gets overlooked in a lot of campervan builds: securing loose items in transit.

Unsecured gear inside a van becomes a projectile under heavy braking or in a collision. A kettle, a cool box, even a heavy book — anything not properly stored can cause real injury. It's one of the reasons drawer systems with positive lockable runners matter so much in a conversion. Drawers that rattle open over bumps, or fly forward under braking, aren't just annoying — they're a genuine safety issue.

What to look for in safe campervan storage:

- Lockable heavy-duty runners (not domestic-grade)
- Positive mechanical latches on locker doors (not just magnets)
- Lightweight items stored high, heavy items low
- Aluminium and phenolic plywood construction for crash and load resilience

All ROAM Systems drawer products use 220 kg lockable runners. Overhead lockers use positive travel latches and Blum soft-close hinges. UK-manufactured and engineered for the loads campervans actually carry.

More on safe storage planning at the link in bio.

It's the small things that decide whether a weekend in the van is restful or stressful.

Knowing where the kettle is. Pulling out a dry pair of socks without unpacking three bags. Stowing a wet jacket somewhere that won't ruin the upholstery. The kind of details you don't think about when you're building the van, but feel every single trip after.

Good storage isn't about cramming more in. It's about knowing where everything lives, getting to it without unpacking the whole van, and trusting that nothing's rattling around behind you on the M5. That's what changes a van from a project into somewhere you actually want to spend a long weekend.

Whatever you're building toward — Snowdonia in October, the Highlands in summer, or just somewhere quiet for a couple of nights — the storage is the bit you'll thank yourself for getting right.
